# Optional numeric field application fixture

The independent oracle separates missing `-` from present signed ASCII i64,
uses explicit range checks and checks every intermediate sum in original
order. It preserves present zero versus missing, accepts the final nonempty
unterminated line, removes only a terminating LF, and rejects empty interior
records or CR/whitespace. Exact output is unquoted LF CSV with one header and
one data row. No production composition/parser implementation is imported.

| Group | Cases | Coverage |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| model | 33 | Empty/all-missing/mixed/present zero, signs/leading zeros, full-width extrema/cancellation, safe intermediates, final EOF/LF, exact 64-byte lines, 1024-byte read boundaries, 65536 records, 1 MiB input and seeded cases |
| rejection | 30 | Empty/control/non-ASCII/malformed/out-of-range fields, ordered overflow despite later cancellation, line/count/byte caps and invalid later records, all with empty stdout |
| cli | 17 | No operands, sole help aliases/input bypass, unknown/mixed/duplicate options and argument byte cap |
| io | 18 | Directory stdin, closed data/help stdout, traced baseline, five reached input/help-owner allocation denials, read/write EINTR, input/required-EOF/output errors, signal failure, 8192-attempt budgets and genuine 10-byte partial output |

Normal no-argument capture has no allocation. Selected ENOMEM faults reach
three input growth sites and both help-argument owners. Each fault must occur
at its selected ordinal, return 4 and publish nothing; successful observed
mappings require explicit same-address/same-size releases. Baseline output
follows actual EOF, and no allocation occurs after EOF. This finite syscall
evidence is not a resource checker, exhaustive campaign, lifetime or leak proof.

The output prefix is generated by a real kernel file-size limit: a regular
stdout file receives `RLIMIT_FSIZE=10` and inherited ignored SIGXFSZ. An
independent Python host probe confirmed an actual 10-byte write followed by
EFBIG before this test was added. The application must return 5 and preserve
exactly the first 10 independently expected CSV bytes. No successful transfer
count is fabricated and the app is not split into writes for the test.
This case is untraced so its limit does not truncate strace evidence; mapping
cleanup is observed separately in the traced output-error controls.

Persistent EINTR uses compact strace summaries: 8192 input calls/errors, or
8192 output errors plus one successful stderr diagnostic write. Those summaries
do not observe allocation releases. Native children have 20-second deadlines;
registered groups have 85-second deadlines. Call quotas are not host deadlines.

```sh
python3 -B tests/fixtures/stdlib_execution/optional_sum/oracle.py controls
python3 -B tests/fixtures/stdlib_execution/optional_sum/oracle.py model PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/stdlib_execution/optional_sum/oracle.py rejection PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/stdlib_execution/optional_sum/oracle.py cli PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/stdlib_execution/optional_sum/oracle.py io PATH_TO_ELF
```

Commands, input, stdout, stderr, exit status and optional syscall traces are
retained. CPU controls include every generated successful numeric reference,
explicit full-width/cancellation values and a deliberately missing release.

## Acceptance

All four registered groups passed: 98 distinct native cases on Linux x86_64.
The driver uses the GPU compiler and shared strict ELF checker before CPU
execution. The receipts are separate runs of the same frozen application and
oracle; the boundary run filters out the model test.

| Receipt in `target/stdlib-work/` | Registered tests | Cases | Runtime | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `outcome-composition-app-model-first.log` | 1 passed | model 33 | 7.26 s | `/tmp/optional-sum-model-8lt2heja` |
| `outcome-composition-app-boundaries-first.log` | 3 passed | cli 17, rejection 30, io 18 | 8.02 s | `/tmp/optional-sum-cli-xa7ywdhk`, `/tmp/optional-sum-rejection-ft6y0iw0`, `/tmp/optional-sum-io-a2lfj7mz` |

Accepted identities (SHA-256):

- Application: `12e4acaedabeb4815d63eab9aabb58d616892f99af6048b14a7b417ef718ae1b`.
- Oracle: `006907de078b05e3185d831ae4d3adb4ea3974e719087d6ed0818e9ff753ef9c`.

The inspected baseline retains 4100 input bytes, observes the required zero-byte
EOF read, releases its final input mapping, then writes the complete 35-byte
CSV. Input allocation denials reached mmap ordinals 1, 3 and 4; help-owner
denials reached ordinals 1 and 2. All five return 4 with empty stdout and release
every successfully observed mapping. Required-EOF EIO after all 4100 input
bytes still publishes nothing. Compact summaries confirm 8192 read errors or
8192 write errors plus the diagnostic write. The file-size-limit case returns
5 with actual file content exactly `present,mi` (10 bytes); it is untraced as
described above.

These observations cover the selected finite paths. Device execution, formal
verification, exhaustive allocation faults and unreachable status-6 invariant
failures remain unclaimed. Driver hashes are omitted because subsequent
whitespace formatting does not change the accepted application or oracle.
